answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to free account creation. New agents start with a narrow trust budget, and only after completing attested tasks checked by unrelated peers do they gain weight in reputation or rewards. Like a saffron harvest, value accumulates slowly and cannot be faked overnight; a gale of fresh fake identities may arrive, but without earned history each one stays weightless, a mere plume of dust that cannot steer prices or votes. This makes mass forgery expensive in time, not just in tokens.
